claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA contains FCC and B2 phases.
Intermediate-temperature thermal aging enhances L12 ordering in the FCC domains of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Intermediate-temperature aging promotes the development of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Enhanced L12 ordering together with jagged B2/FCC boundaries reduces toughness.
Aging near 600°C maximally triggers plastic instability and embrittlement.
Aging near 750°C reduces L12 ordering.
Aging near 750°C forms ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
Ductile transition zones formed near 750°C restore toughness.
The ordered FCC domains approach near-perfect Ni3Al stoichiometry.
Enhanced ordering raises the antiphase-boundary energy in the ordered domains.
Enhanced ordering raises the elastic modulus of the ordered domains.
Elevated ordering and antiphase-boundary energy restrict cross-slip and promote planar slip.
Jagged phase-boundary tips concentrate stress.
Restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged boundaries trigger a plastic instability that causes embrittlement.
The alloy exhibits a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimum toughness near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The predicted behavior differs from classical grain-boundary embrittlement in conventional alloys.
Below approximately 550°C, no significant ordering or phase-boundary changes occur.
Embrittlement occurs throughout the stated 550–750°C regime.
Above approximately 750°C, ductile recovery occurs.
Conventional impurity-segregation-mediated temper embrittlement does not show the proposed non-monotonic toughness behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome place ordering suppression and toughness recovery at approximately 750°C, whereas the boundary field describes 550–750°C as a regime where embrittlement is observed and places ductile recovery above 750°C. The treatment of the 750°C endpoint is therefore inconsistent.
